withdrawnFinding.reason: The lead diagnosis is correct and was re-verified here. The second JobAttemptFaulted belongs to the new RetryAttempt 1, not to the previous attempt. Its status check was immediately due because the test never reset the Quartz offset, and JobAttemptStateMachine treats a status check in Starting as a start timeout of the current attempt. GetRetryDelay then returns null because RetryAttempt 1 is not below SuspectJobRetryCount 1.
withdrawnFinding.myError: I attributed the second fault to the previous attempt without ever checking its AttemptId.

testClockCorrection: The suspect fault is now held inside the test local receive filter before next.Send. The test observes that barrier, puts the Quartz offset back by 60 seconds and only then releases the fault, so the reset can never race the forwarding.

positiveProof.provenChain: two suppressions of the same MessageId on job and job-attempt, no redelivery, no consumer retry, no Fault<JobAttemptFaulted>, status checks, Running to CheckingStatus to Suspect, JobAttemptFaulted with RetryDelay, RetryAttempt 1, Completed, and no terminal JobFaulted

staleAttemptProbe.determinism: The retry attempt is held inside its own consumer until all three late terminal messages of the previous attempt have provably reached the job saga. An earlier version of this probe was green by timing alone and is discarded.
staleAttemptProbe.conclusion: The hypothesis that a late terminal message of a previous attempt changes the running attempt is excluded for these three events: the job still completes on RetryAttempt 1, and neither JobFaulted nor JobCanceled is published.
staleAttemptProbe.staticCheckOfStarted: JobStateMachine guards progress and state messages with context.Saga.AttemptId == context.Message.AttemptId, while the AttemptStarted, AttemptCompleted, AttemptFaulted and AttemptCanceled handlers carry no such guard. The dynamic probe shows this has no effect on the outcome for the three terminal events.

separateObservation.statement: A late JobAttemptFaulted of a previous attempt is rejected by the job saga with NotAcceptedStateMachineException and redelivered by the retry policy on the job endpoint. It does not change the running attempt, which the probe proves, but the rejection and its redelivery are visible in the log.
